I have already performed two searches: one for “2026 small language model training recipe state of the art efficient” and another for “2025 2026 on-policy distillation reasoning small models RL recipe”. The results from those queries gave me a handful of recent papers about distillation, pre‑training recipes, and agentic tool calling. However, the user’s request is broader: they want more recent and useful papers, not just about training recipes but also about architectural advances that could boost capability in a tiny model. 

Looking through the existing search results, I notice that many of the top hits are about distillation and data efficiency, but I’m missing newer work on memory‑augmented transformers, sparse knowledge storage, and other mechanisms that have shown promise for scaling knowledge capacity without increasing parameters. The earlier part of the conversation also referenced “memory layers” and “product‑key memory” as promising avenues for small models. The user’s feedback suggests they want fresh, cutting‑edge research that could be directly incorporated into our design.

Thus, the next logical step is to broaden the literature search to specifically target recent papers (2025‑2026) that discuss memory layers, sparse knowledge storage, and transformer scaling techniques. This will complement the existing set of papers on data quality and distillation, and give us a more complete, up‑to‑date bibliography to feed into the research markdown file.

I will issue a new web search query focusing on “2026 memory layers sparse knowledge storage transformer scaling”. This phrasing captures the key concepts (memory layers, sparsity, knowledge storage) and restricts results to the most recent year, increasing the chance of finding the latest relevant arXiv submissions. This aligns with the user’s request for more recent and useful papers, and will provide the needed material for the next update to the research.md file.
